title: mcp-doctor fixture cases
description: The specification expressed as examples. Both implementations run every case and must agree.
$comment: TWO RUNS PER CASE. `expect.scan` is a read-only run; `expect.fix` is a --fix run. They are
separate because they answer different questions, and a corpus that conflates them cannot
prove that scanning changes nothing or that fixing reports what it changed.
EXACT BYTES. Inputs are `raw_files` — literal file content, not JSON objects — and
`expect.fix.files` is the literal expected content afterwards. Asserting on parsed FIELDS
would let two implementations reformat differently and both 'pass', which is exactly the
drift the conformance suite exists to catch. Byte equality is also the only way to prove
the span-edit model (PLAN D6) preserves comments, CRLF and BOM.
`expect.fix` is SKIPPED by the harness when the client is not write-capable on the running
OS. The fixtures still describe the target behaviour, so they are written before the
capability is enabled rather than after.

client.$comment: Must match a registry entry id.

raw_files.description: path → exact bytes. Always literal: formatting, comments, line endings and any BOM are part of the fixture.

env.description: Variable → value; null means explicitly unset for this case.

scan_expectation.description: A read-only run. It must never modify a file, which the harness asserts for every case without needing to be told.

findings.description: Findings that MUST be present. Order-independent.

must_not_contain_findings.description: Findings that MUST NOT appear — how a short-circuit like the host rule is proven.

no_network_to.description: Hosts the run must never contact. Asserted by the fake transport.

fix_expectation.description: A --fix run. Exactly one of `files` or `files_unchanged` is required: either we know the resulting bytes, or we are asserting there are none.

findings.description: Findings reported AFTER the fix. A repaired defect appears with fixed=true; an unrepairable one persists.

files.description: path → exact expected bytes after the fix. Every other byte in the file must be untouched.

files_unchanged.description: Every file must remain byte-identical. This is how the host rule stops being a promise.

backup_expected.description: Whether a timestamped .bak must exist afterwards. False when nothing was written.
